assumptions: 'giant functions' means stacks too long or too deep, not literal line count
'missing error handling' means external api.request calls not wrapped in try_catch, the only error-handling check the catalogue has
the workspace's endpoints and functions are in scope for all three; no api_groups/tags scoping since the workspace has almost no tags
advisory and active per brief for a new policy; no blocking requested
policy keys reuse the template keys CHG-001, LOG-010, CONV-040
workspace_names_used: function/acme_get_tracking.xs (only file with try_catch around api.request)
workflow_test/invoices_require_login.xs, workflow_test/health_check.xs (only two tests in workspace)
tags public, smoke (no owner or sensitivity tags exist)
confusions: CHG-001 template scopes object.test_coverage to object_kinds ['query'] but the ask covers functions too; unclear whether a template's rules are a starting point or a fixed set, and the catalogue entry for test_coverage did not list object_kinds in its params section I read
CONV-040 and CONV-041 are the same check with different params; the skill says a template is one policy with its key, so merging two templates into one rule was my call and not documented
xano policy parse text output dropped the severity line for LOG-010 while printing it for CHG-001 and CONV-040; the -o json output shows severity medium. I used json to confirm

the skill says the catalogue is the entire vocabulary but the template table lists 'tests' as CHG-001 with severity low, which seems mismatched with a customer asking to stop breaking prod; no guidance on severity choice
no guidance for 'missing error handling' in general: only external-call containment has a check, and the fix note (add try_catch) is only for external calls
wished_for: a check that counts lines or a size proxy the customer would recognise, or a recipe mapping 'long functions' to stack.size_limit
a recipe for combining two templates into one policy (e.g. CONV-040 + CONV-041)
a check that tests assertion content, or at least a note on what an assertion must check
guidance on error handling for DB writes and logic, not just api.request
an example policy showing object_kinds usage in test_coverage and size_limit (the templates list them but the check docs do not confirm the param names)
why_confidence: Each of the three rules maps to a real catalogue check and parses with no rule warnings, but the goal is partly met: error handling is covered only for external calls, test checks prove presence not quality, and '200 line functions' is approximated by statements and nesting. The policies are advisory and not yet evaluated against the workspace, so the predicted findings are unverified.
